content_units: Corporate L&D Pivot: Best-Fit Direction

You already have a strong foundation for   Learning & Development, instructional design, facilitation, and training delivery  . With 7 years of teaching, lesson design, LMS use, and some Storyline exposure, your most realistic first-step targets are   L&D Specialist  ,   Instructional Designer  ,   Learning Designer  , and   Trainer/Facilitator   roles rather than senior strategic roles like Head of L&D.
For   Dublin or EU-remote   and a   €55,000+ goal  , the best positioning is:
-   Primary lane:   Instructional Designer / Learning Designer
-   Secondary lane:   Learning & Development Specialist / Training Specialist
-   Stretch lane:   Enablement or Program roles if paired with stronger business metrics and stakeholder language
Job Titles to Search and Priority Fit
Job Title   Fit for Your Background   Salary Potential vs €55k   Why It Fits
Instructional Designer   High   Strong   Closest match to lesson design, curriculum building, LMS, Storyline
Learning Designer   High   Strong   Common title in tech, consulting, and higher-growth firms
Learning & Development Specialist   High   Moderate-Strong   Good transition title for teachers moving into corporate L&D
Learning Experience Designer   Medium-High   Strong   Useful if roles emphasize digital learning journeys and learner engagement
Training Specialist   High   Moderate   Great if delivery/facilitation is prominent
Training Facilitator / Corporate Trainer   High   Moderate   Best if you want live workshops and onboarding-focused roles
LMS Administrator / Learning Systems Specialist   Medium   Moderate   Viable if your LMS experience is deeper than average
Best search strings
Use combinations like:
- `"Instructional Designer" Dublin`
- `"Learning Designer" Ireland`
- `"L&D Specialist" Dublin`
- `"Training Specialist" Dublin`
- `"Corporate Trainer" Ireland remote`
- `"Learning Experience Designer" EU remote`
- `"Enablement Specialist" remote Europe`
- `"Sales Enablement Trainer" remote EU`
- `"Onboarding Specialist" learning Dublin`
Roles to treat as stretch targets
These can still be worth applying to selectively:
- Learning Business Partner
- Senior Instructional Designer
- Learning Program Manager
- Talent Development Specialist
- Enablement Manager
Your Transferable Strengths in Corporate Language
Option 1:   Learning design and curriculum development     You already build structured learning experiences from outcomes backward   Strongest asset
Use on CV
Option 2:   Facilitation and stakeholder-facing delivery     Classroom teaching translates directly to workshop delivery, learner engagement, and live training   High-value for trainer/L&D roles
Target trainer roles
Option 3:   Assessment and learning effectiveness     You measure learner progress, adapt instruction, and improve results based on evidence   Useful for corporate evaluation language
Add metrics
Option 4:   LMS and digital learning tools     LMS use plus basic Storyline gives you credibility for blended and e-learning roles   Good bridge into instructional design
Build portfolio
How to translate teaching into corporate wording
Instead of school-centered phrasing, use:
- “Designed and delivered learning programs” instead of “taught classes”
- “Facilitated instructor-led and blended learning” instead of “ran lessons”
- “Created assessment strategies to measure learning outcomes” instead of “graded students”
- “Managed learning delivery across multiple cohorts” instead of “taught multiple classes”
- “Used LMS platforms to assign, track, and evaluate learner progress” instead of “posted homework online”
- “Adapted content for varied learner needs and performance levels” instead of “differentiated instruction”
First Gaps to Close for a €55k+ Move
The biggest barrier is usually   not capability   but   corporate proof  . Close the gaps that hiring managers care about first:
Priority 1: Build a corporate-facing portfolio
- Create 2–3 samples:
- One   Storyline microlearning module
- One   ILT/VILT facilitator guide + slide deck
- One   blended program outline   with objectives, activities, and evaluation plan
- Make the topics business-oriented: onboarding, compliance, communication, manager coaching, product basics
Priority 2: Learn corporate L&D frameworks and vocabulary
Focus on:
- ADDIE
- Adult learning principles / andragogy
- Kirkpatrick evaluation model
- Needs analysis / training needs analysis
- Learning objectives tied to business outcomes
- SME collaboration and stakeholder management
Priority 3: Strengthen Storyline and one adjacent tool
